title: Co-Evolution of Large Language Models and Configuration Strategies to Enhance Surrogate-Assisted Evolutionary Algorithm

problem.claim: Surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms optimize computationally expensive black-box problems, but their sample efficiency depends heavily on configuring the surrogate model and sampling criteria.

gap.claim: Manual configuration of core surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithm components requires substantial effort and expert knowledge, limiting broader applicability.

contributions.claim: CoE-SAEA co-evolves large language models and configuration strategies to enhance surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms.
CoE-SAEA uses three populations to evolve LLM prompts, optimize configuration strategies, and solve the optimization problem with the selected algorithm configuration.
CoE-SAEA includes an exploration-exploitation module that chooses between exploring new LLM-generated configuration strategies and exploiting existing strategies.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CoE-SAEA as a novel paradigm for co-evolving LLMs and configuration strategies to enhance surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report empirical validation against state-of-the-art algorithms across various benchmark problems and a real-world traffic signal optimization task.
The authors report that the proposed CoE-SAEA source code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: SAEAs are presented as suitable for computationally expensive black-box optimization.
SAEA sample efficiency depends on surrogate-model and sampling-criteria configuration, while manual configuration limits applicability.
CoE-SAEA is proposed as a co-evolutionary paradigm combining LLMs with configuration strategies.
The paradigm uses three role-specific populations and an exploration-exploitation module.
The authors report comparisons with state-of-the-art algorithms on benchmark problems and a traffic signal optimization task.

source_observation.claim: The approach separates prompt evolution, configuration-strategy optimization, and optimization execution into distinct populations.

interpretation.claim: Separating instruction generation, strategy search, and task execution may clarify roles in automated algorithm configuration.

application.claim: Use role-specific search processes when an optimization workflow combines language-model guidance with algorithm configuration.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation improves performance across settings beyond the reported evaluation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark problems, compared algorithms, datasets, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the LLMs, surrogate models, configuration strategies, or exploration-exploitation decision rule in detail.
The abstract does not provide implementation, computational-cost, ablation, or reproducibility details beyond the source-code availability statement.
